item.title: Kunisaki Peninsula — Guide
item.description: The Kunisaki Peninsula, a rounded, mountainous headland in northeastern Oita, is one of Japan’s most atmospheric and spiritually rich rural regions. Its rugged volcanic landscape of forested ridges and deep valleys became, over a thousand years ago, the cradle of a unique syncretic Buddhist-Shinto culture known as Rokugō Manzan, blending the worship of Usa’s Hachiman deity with mountain Buddhism. The peninsula is dotted with ancient temples, weathered stone pagodas, Niō guardian statues and dramatic Buddhist images carved into cliff faces, many hidden deep in the mountains and reached by atmospheric hiking trails.
